panels.description:
This panel provides a high-level summary of current Kubernetes cluster activity through key metrics:
Total Pods: total number of pods running across the cluster.
Namespace Pods: number of pods running in the scientific-workflow namespace.
Total Nodes: number of nodes currently registered in the cluster.
Running Workflows: number of active Argo workflows currently in progress.

This panel shows a breakdown of memory usage and capacity for the selected node:
Total Memory: Total memory available for pods after reserving resources for the system.
Usage: Current working set memory used by all containers (excluding inactive memory).
Requests: Total memory requested by all containers on the node.
Limits: Total memory limits defined for all containers.
panels.title: Node Memory Information

panels.description:
This panel shows how CPU resources are being used and allocated on the selected node, relative to its total allocatable CPU:
CPU Utilization Rate (%): Real-time CPU usage by all containers, based on a 2-minute rate.
CPU Request Rate (%): Total requested CPU resources by containers.
CPU Limit Rate (%): Total CPU limits defined for containers.
panels.title: Node CPU Ratio

panels.description:
This panel provides an overview of pod capacity and usage:
Number of nodes: Number of nodes in the cluster.
Pod Number of nodes: Number of pods scheduled on the selected node (excluding Jobs and unspecified owners).
Upper limit Pod: Maximum number of pods the selected node can run, based on its allocatable resources.
panels.title: Nodes with Pod

panels.description:
This panel shows how memory resources are used and allocated on the selected node, as a percentage of its allocatable memory:
Memory Utilization: Actual memory used by running containers (working set).
Memory Request Rate: Total memory requested by all scheduled containers.
Memory Limit Rate: Total memory limits defined for those containers.
panels.title: Node Memory Ratio

panels.description:
This panel shows the actual CPU usage and allocation on the selected node, measured in CPU cores:
Total Cores: Total number of CPU cores available for pods on the node.
Usage: Real-time CPU usage based on a 2-minute rate (container_cpu_usage_seconds_total).
Requests: Total CPU cores requested by all scheduled containers.
Limit: Total CPU core limits defined for containers.
panels.title: Node CPU Number of cores

panels.description:
This panel shows the disk usage status of the /var mountpoint across all nodes:
Utilization Rate: Percentage of used space on /var.
Usage: Total used disk space on /var.
Total: Total available disk space on /var.

Should be adjusted when deployed to an actual HPC cluster to ensure that thee main mountpoint of the filesystem is used
panels.title: Node Storage Information

panels.description:
This panel shows the current network traffic for the selected node and namespace:
Receive: Rate of incoming network data (in bits per second).
Send: Rate of outgoing network data (in bits per second).
panels.title: $NameSpace：Network Overview（Associable nodes and namespaces）

panels.description:
This panel displays memory usage and allocation details for the selected node, in raw byte values:
Total Memory: Total memory available for pods on the node.
Usage: Current working set memory used by all running containers.
Requests: Total memory requested by containers scheduled on the node.
Limit: Total memory limits defined for those containers.
panels.title: Memory Usage【$Node】

panels.description:
This panel shows CPU resource data for the selected node, measured in core units:
Total cores: Total CPU cores available for pod scheduling on the node.
Usage: Real-time CPU usage, based on a 2-minute rate of active CPU time.
Requests: Total CPU cores requested by all scheduled containers.
Limit: Total CPU core limits set for those containers.
panels.title: CPU Used Cores【$Node】

panels.description:
This panel provides an overview of pod capacity and usage in the cluster:
Number of nodes: Number of nodes currently available in the cluster.
Pod number: Number of active pods on the selected node (excluding Jobs and unowned pods).
Upper limit pod: Maximum number of pods the selected node can run, based on its allocatable resources.
panels.title: Pod Number and nodes【$Node】

panels.description: This graph shows the CPU usage of each container as a percentage of its defined CPU limit over a selected period of time.

targets.expr:
max(
  irate(container_cpu_usage_seconds_total{
    pod=~"$Pod",
    container=~"$Container",
    container!="",
    container!="POD",
    node=~"^$Node$",
    namespace=~"$NameSpace"
  }[2m])
) by (container, pod)
/ 
max(
  kube_pod_container_resource_limits{
    resource="cpu",
    unit="core",
    pod=~"$Pod",
    container=~"$Container",
    namespace=~"$NameSpace"
  }
) by (container, pod)
* 100

panels.title: Pod Containers CPU Utilization ( Maximum 100% Associable Nodes)

panels.description: This panel shows how much “in-use” memory (excluding cache) is being consumed relative to the container’s memory limit by different pods

targets.expr:
max(
  container_memory_working_set_bytes{
    origin_prometheus=~"$origin_prometheus",
    pod=~"$Pod",
    container=~"$Container",
    container!="", container!="POD",
    node=~"^$Node$",
    namespace=~"$NameSpace"
  }
) by (container, pod)
/ 
max(
  kube_pod_container_resource_limits{
    origin_prometheus=~"$origin_prometheus",
    pod=~"$Pod",
    container=~"$Container",
    resource="memory",
    unit="byte",
    namespace=~"$NameSpace"
  }
) by (container, pod)
* 100

panels.title: Pod Container Memory Usage (Associatable Nodes)

panels.description:
This panel shows the network activity of containers in bits per second (bps), broken down per pod:
Inflow: The rate at which each container receives data from the network.
Outflow: The rate at which each container sends data over the network.
panels.title: Pod Network bandwidth per second (Associable Nodes)

panels.description: This panel shows how much CPU each container is using, alongside its CPU limit. It is visible which containers are consuming a lot of CPU and how close they are to hitting their limit.
panels.title: Pod Containers CPU Core Usage

panels.description: This panel shows how much memory each container is using, compared to its configured memory limit.
panels.title: Pod Containers WSS Memory Usage (Associable Nodes)

panels.description: This panel shows the Resident Set Size (RSS) memory used by each container. RSS represents the portion of memory that is actively used and held in RAM (not cached or swapped).
panels.title: Pod Containers RSS Memory Usage (Associable Nodes)
